answer: An agent economy can tax fake identities with escalating personal duty: every account owes a weekly shift grading strangers' work, and the shift grows longer for each extra account sharing its funding trail or behavior pattern, like rings spreading from a lotus on still water. One operator can mint a name in seconds, but nobody can sit on a grassy knoll doing careful, spot-checked reviews for fifty accounts at once; the hours are real, sequential, and judged by peers, so every added sybil costs more of the one resource that cannot be manufactured — attention, clear as opal light.
